summary: Ukrainian long-range drones struck major Russian energy infrastructure including the Kstovo refinery and Wildberries warehouses, while Russian forces intensified attacks on Ukrainian cities with guided bombs and ballistic missiles causing civilian casualties. CIA Director Ratcliffe visited Moscow amid U.S. requests for Ukraine to pause strikes on Russian territory. Ukrainian forces regained ground near Zakhidne as shell supply chains extend into 2027.
key_points: Ukrainian drones hit LUKOIL Kstovo refinery (17M tons/year capacity) and Wildberries logistics centers in Kotovsk and Tambov region. (Source: @eRadarrua/107150)
Russian KAB strikes on Kramatorsk injured 24 including an infant; drone attacks hit Chernihiv and Zaporizhzhia. (Source: @UkraineNow/83681)
CIA Director Ratcliffe arrived in Moscow; U.S. asked Ukraine not to attack Moscow or St. Petersburg during visit. (Source: @UkraineNow/83693)
Ukraine received Patriot missiles, AIM-120 AMRAAM, and Crotale air defense systems per Zelensky. (Source: @UkraineNow/83680)
Russian Iskander-M and Zircon missile threats detected from Taganrog and Sumy region toward Poltava and Chernihiv. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/71015)
Ukrainian forces restored control near Zakhidne per DeepState map update. (Source: @DeepStateUA/23778)
Shell supply chain: 530k 155mm shells contracted via Romania with Serbian components, deliveries planned through spring 2027. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32725)
EU has no plans to reopen frozen Russian asset discussions for Ukraine financing. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32737)

sections.threat_assessment: Russian forces are escalating combined strikes using guided bombs, ballistic missiles (Iskander-M, Zircon), and drones against Ukrainian population centers and infrastructure, causing mounting civilian casualties. Ukrainian long-range drone campaigns are systematically degrading Russian energy and logistics infrastructure deep inside Russia, including major refineries and supply depots. The CIA director's Moscow visit and U.S. requests for strike pauses indicate active diplomatic maneuvering amid battlefield escalation. Ukrainian air defense is being bolstered with Western systems but faces saturation from multi-axis missile and drone threats. The extended shell supply chain through 2027 signals Western preparation for prolonged conflict.
sections.regional_response: Kazakhstan agreed to process Russian oil and return 70% of refined products to Russia, maintaining energy cooperation despite sanctions. The EU remains deadlocked on using frozen Russian assets for Ukraine, with no plans to reopen discussions. China's Xi Jinping congratulated Zelensky on Independence Day, with Zelensky urging a stronger Chinese diplomatic role. Belarus hosts Russian Su-30 operations near Ukraine's northern border. Regional actors are balancing economic ties with Russia against Western pressure, while diplomatic channels remain active but inconclusive.
sections.intelligence_notes: The Serbian connection in the shell supply chain (Focus Strategies, Emir Smazhilovich) reveals a complex sanctions evasion network linking Serbian, British, American, and Canadian entities. Russian reconnaissance operations in occupied Druzhkivka demonstrate persistent human intelligence capability behind Ukrainian lines. The Amur gas chemical complex fire (123 injured, 1 Chinese contractor killed) suggests either Ukrainian strike or industrial accident at strategic energy infrastructure. Ukrainian domestic tensions evident in Ternopil recruitment center protests. High Telegram trust (73%) indicates information space fragmentation affecting mobilization and morale.
